---
applyTo: "packages/webpack/runtime-config-webpack-plugin/**/*"
---

Keep `RuntimeConfigWebpackPlugin`, its runtime module, and runtime-config integration fixtures in this standalone package rather than exporting or testing them through a DSL-specific webpack plugin. Keep its public options and package dependencies DSL-neutral: accept arbitrary top-level runtime configuration without naming React-specific fields or depending on `@lynx-js/react`. Apply the plugin only to a host compilation; lazy and external bundles consume the page-scoped configuration injected by the host. On each host entry evaluation, assign a fresh configuration object to `lynx.__runtime_configs__` rather than merging into the previous object. Drop stale keys and values from previous evaluations and leave the new object mutable. Keep integration fixtures minimal and DSL-neutral: cover injection into an empty page config and replacement of an existing page config. Direct runtime-module regressions should evaluate generated code twice, mutate and freeze the first config between evaluations, and verify that the second evaluation replaces it with only the current bundle's values. Each fixture must establish its own initial `lynx.__runtime_configs__` state because the test environment can be shared across cases and directory renames can change execution order. Tests import the built `lib` entry, so rebuild through Turbo before interpreting fixture results.
